clue.text: Technical equipment to probe underground

parts.note: to probe something is to test it
the Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground railway

explanation.surface: Engineers need specialist kit to investigate what lies beneath the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground' looks like part of the definition but supplies the London railway's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory glass cylinder is a basic piece of scientific apparatus, loosely technical equipment.

clue.text: Brittle Scottish favourite fit to enter motorbike races

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so the word for fit goes between the race letters

parts.note: the TT races are the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorbike races
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A favourite Scot fit enough to take part in motorbike races.
explanation.walkthrough: Scottish tablet is a crumbly sugar confection, like hard fudge. The TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: This crumbly sweet of sugar, butter and condensed milk is a beloved Scottish confection.

clue.text: Embarrassed fake news boss

parts.note: a sham is a fake
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is left red-faced over fake news.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put to shame is to be humiliated, a near synonym.

clue.text: It's used to observe select abuse, given the rise of EPO

indicators.note: abuse means mistreat, so these letters are knocked into a new order
the rise of means the letters go upwards, read backwards in a down clue

explanation.surface: Something meant to watch for drug abuse in sport, given increasing EPO use.
explanation.walkthrough: EPO is erythropoietin, a doping drug in cycling. 'abuse' rearranges SELECT into TELESC; 'rise of' turns EPO into OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical instrument for viewing distant objects is a device for observing.

clue.text: Hope dear Corbyn turns out to be squeaky clean!

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned and come out differently

explanation.surface: Supporters hope Jeremy Corbyn will prove to have an untarnished record.
explanation.definitionFit: Unblemished in reputation, with nothing to criticise, is the idiomatic sense of squeaky clean.

clue.text: Bill touring Long Kesh, gobsmacked

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the bill's letters go round the prison's name

parts.note: an advertisement, or ad, is a bill posted up
Long Kesh was the Northern Ireland prison better known as the Maze

explanation.surface: Someone is left astonished after a bill or politician visits a notorious Northern Irish prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests a politician or a law, but it is AD, the advert. Long Kesh was the Maze prison near Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly astonished, a close synonym.

clue.text: Mike really excited to see bloke from Genesis

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: A fan is thrilled to meet Mike Rutherford of the band Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis looks like the band (Mike Rutherford was a member) but is the book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Magog appears in Genesis 10 as a son of Japheth, a biblical man.

clue.text: South Africa anger as Nigerian leader imprisoned old Congolese people

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
ire is anger

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so the leading letter sits within the small word
leader means the first letter

explanation.surface: South Africa is outraged when a Nigerian leader is jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire was the former name of the Democratic Republic of Congo, so its citizens were once called this.

clue.text: Order to remove body from graveyard is interrupted

definitions.note: an instruction to dig up a corpse; the answer is an imperative verb

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An exhumation order from a graveyard is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is found across graveyarD IS INTERrupted; read as a command it is an order.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume a corpse is to dig it up, and the bare verb works as a command.

clue.text: Reels in courtroom: midnight, 3rd. of June, Germany, arrested, drunk

parts.note: midnight is twelve o'clock

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the single letter is captured inside the country
drunk means reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order
3rd. of means the third letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A list of courtroom evidence: midnight, June 3rd, a German arrested drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' puts N inside GERMANY, and 'drunk' rearranges the result into ANGRYMEN. 'Reels' means film reels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Lumet's 1957 film is set almost entirely in a jury room, a courtroom drama on reels.

clue.text: Belgian's wry dig wound up mounted knight

indicators.note: wound up suggests something twisted round, so these letters are coiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Belgian's sardonic jibe riled a knight on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belgian's wry dig' is all fodder, apostrophe S included; 'wound up' signals the anagram, not annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tour de France winner was knighted, and a cyclist is mounted on a bike, so he is a knight in the saddle.

clue.text: See 10
The odds of Boris never making a U-turn?

indicators.note: making a U-turn says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wry bet on whether Boris Johnson would ever change his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money is a betting price, the odds offered when win and loss are equally likely.

clue.text: Shade of African flower, but not The Purple Rose of Cairo!

definitions.text: Shade of African flower, but not The Purple Rose of Cairo!

parts.words: Shade of African flower, but not The Purple Rose of Cairo!
parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the African river through Cairo gives a colour that is not purple

explanation.surface: A colour question that plays on Woody Allen's film The Purple Rose of Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, a crossword trick for river; the river through Cairo names a pale bluish-green colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale green colour is named after the great African river, so it is that river's shade.

clue.text: In a daze, old Freud traduced the Gallic race

indicators.note: In tells us the remaining letters sit inside the word for a daze

parts.note: a daze is a trance

indicators.note: traduced means misrepresented, so these letters are rendered in a false order

explanation.surface: Sigmund Freud, dazed, slanders the French as a people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traduced' makes OURDEF, which 'In' sets inside the word for a daze. 'race' is a cycling race, not an ethnic group.
explanation.definitionFit: The great French cycle race is literally the Tour of France, the Gallic race.

clue.text: Refund Earl following massage upset in bubbly French spa

indicators.note: following puts the nobleman's letter after the rest
in places the turned-round letters inside the town's name

parts.note: Reims is a French spa town in the Champagne region, famous for bubbly

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned up, the letters read backwards

parts.note: to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: An earl, unhappy with a massage at a French spa, wants his money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the massage word round and 'in' sets it within the Champagne town; 'bubbly' is a description, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To refund is to pay money back, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Told to purchase drug for use between legs of 14

indicators.note: Told signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: buy crack: to purchase the drug crack cocaine

explanation.surface: Someone is told to buy drugs to use between their legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legs' means stages of the Tour de France at 14, between which bikes are stored on racks or roof carriers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack holding bicycles is used between stages of a cycle race.

clue.text: Breeding ground for storm in Berlin about rise of right-wing party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the German word goes round the party

parts.note: Sturm is German for storm

indicators.note: rise of in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: AfD, Alternative for Germany, a right-wing German party

explanation.surface: A storm brews in Berlin as the far right rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm where horses are bred is a place for breeding stock.

clue.text: Out and about, trying to get a claret jug to display

parts.words: trying to get a claret jug
parts.note: the Claret Jug is the trophy for golf's Open Championship, so a golfer chasing it is playing in that event
to air something is to display it

explanation.surface: A golfer competing for the Claret Jug is outdoors, showing off the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The Claret Jug is the trophy of golf's Open Championship, not a wine pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outdoors, outside under the sky, is to be out and about.

clue.text: Prize top chicken, cow

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A cowardly hen and a cow win prizes at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' and 'cow' look like farm animals; only the cow is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tour de France leader wears this prized garment, a top worth winning.

clue.text: See 19
Morse code manoeuvred, unopened

indicators.note: code as an imperative tells us to encode, scramble, the letters that follow
unopened means the first letter is removed from the word

explanation.surface: A message in Morse code was skilfully manipulated but never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse code' reads as one phrase but splits: Morse is the definition, 'code' the anagram signal on MANOEUVRED minus its opening M.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse in Colin Dexter's novels had the rarely used first name Endeavour.

clue.text: A row about money management

indicators.note: about means around, so the noise goes round the money letter

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: A quarrel over money in the business.
explanation.definitionFit: Administration is the running of an organisation, so a synonym of management.

clue.text: Bishop, head of episcopate, penning vicar a longish note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so these letters hold the clergyman inside them

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A bishop and an episcopal leader, holding a vicar, write a fairly long memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a letter or memo but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a breve is a note twice the length of a semibreve, so longish indeed.

clue.text: Adult cinema production not gory enough

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in old film certificates

indicators.note: a production reworks the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An adult film was dismissed by its audience as too tame on the bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' sounds like film-making but rearranges CINEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking blood, literally pale and feeble, is a witty take on insufficiently gory.

clue.text: The Stones; men embracing R&B

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the musical genre goes within

parts.note: males are men
rhythm and blues, written RB without the ampersand

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones are a band of men steeped in rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Stones' suggests the band but means stones generally, e.g. the Elgin sculptures or glass spheres.
explanation.definitionFit: These small glass balls, or carved sculptures like the Elgin set, are stones in a looser sense.

clue.text: Japanese cover for Yoko's follow-up to Rocket Man

indicators.note: follow-up to says the surname comes after the other name

parts.note: Rocket Man was Donald Trump's nickname for North Korea's leader Kim Jong-un
Yoko Ono, John Lennon's widow

explanation.surface: Yoko Ono releases a cover version as the sequel to Elton John's Rocket Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket Man' looks like the Elton John song but is Kim Jong-un; 'cover' looks musical but is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Japanese robe is a garment that covers the body.

clue.text: In train in tunnel?

definitions.meaning: in train means in progress, already begun
a tunnel runs beneath a road, beneath the way

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a train is in a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: Already in progress, as a plan in train is; and literally below the road.
